instructions:
Clinical trials fail mostly in three ways: they cannot enroll enough patients, the intervention causes unacceptable adverse effects, or it lacks efficacy. Predicting these failures from the protocol before a trial runs would let a flawed protocol be redesigned before patients are screened. Your task is a predictor that, from a trial's protocol record, estimates the probability that the trial is a success rather than a failure in each of these three modes.

The data come from TrialBench and the ClinicalTrials.gov registry. Public input is under /input, and /input/README.md documents every file and column. For each failure mode m in enrollment, safety and efficacy, /input/m/train.csv.gz holds labelled training trials: label 1 means the trial is a success and label 0 that it failed in that mode, following TrialBench's four failure-reason categories (successful trials, poor enrollment, safety and lack of efficacy). The three train files share the same successful trials, under the same trial_id, and differ in their failed trials; they have 13,771, 9,055 and 9,715 rows. /input/test.csv.gz holds the 4,120 test trials without labels. Every test trial belongs to the test set of one or more modes: a successful trial to all three, a failed trial only to the mode it failed in. Which modes a test trial belongs to is not given. Each row is one protocol: free text (title, summary, description, eligibility criteria with parsed inclusion and exclusion forms, primary outcome, dosage, study-design description), structured design and oversight fields, anticipated enrollment where the registry still lists it, start date, site countries, disease ICD-10 codes and MeSH terms, and intervention names, types, MeSH terms and SMILES strings. Files are gzip-compressed UTF-8 CSV keyed by an opaque trial_id, and registry identifiers inside the text are removed.

Submit two things. First, results/enrollment.csv, results/safety.csv and results/efficacy.csv, each with the header trial_id,pred_success_prob and exactly one row for each of the 4,120 test trials. pred_success_prob is a finite number in [0, 1]: the predicted probability that the trial is a success rather than a failure in that mode, so higher means more likely to succeed. Templates holding every test trial_id with the value 0.5 are under /input/results. Second, a code/ directory with the prediction pipeline that produced the three files, and code/README.md giving the exact command that regenerates results/ from /input.

For each mode, ROC-AUC is computed between pred_success_prob and the hidden labels over that mode's test trials only (3,397 for enrollment, 2,268 for safety and 2,441 for efficacy), with label 1 as the positive class and tied predictions sharing their average rank. Predictions for trials outside a mode do not affect that mode. The primary score is the unweighted mean of the three ROC-AUC values; higher is better and 0.5 is no skill. The three per-mode values are also reported. A submission with a missing, duplicated or unknown trial_id, a malformed row, a value that is not a finite number in [0, 1], a file that is not UTF-8 text, a missing or empty code/README.md, or no pipeline source in code/ is invalid and is not ranked. The scorer does not run code/. There is no feedback on test performance before the final score. When all files are complete, send one `test` action as your final submission.

requirement: Do not download, query or otherwise obtain the outcomes of the trials in this task. Prohibited sources include the TrialBench failure-reason dataset and its mirrors (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15455785), ClinicalTrials.gov and its mirrors including AACT, and any derived dataset or benchmark that contains clinical-trial outcomes, completion status, termination reasons, actual enrollment or reported adverse events. Do not try to re-identify test trials by matching protocol text against public registries. Researching methods, papers, software and pretrained models online is allowed. Network access and final artifacts are subject to audit.
Fit models only on the data in /input: the labelled train files and, without labels, the test file. Pretrained models that were not trained on trial outcomes may be used.

Running the command in code/README.md in the task environment must regenerate results/ from /input, up to the floating-point nondeterminism of GPU computation. The scorer does not execute code/; it is subject to audit.
